lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg shifted in front of Ninsun, placing his body between her and the archive door. In the dark, the movement was nearly silent. Only the leather wrapping on his spear gave a faint creak beneath his grip.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun held Ammaru's ledger tablet against her chest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo stood beside the lowest shelf with her knife angled down along her forearm, hidden from anyone entering above. Zeek remained near the foot of the steps, close enough to see the thin line of light beneath the door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rain drummed against the roof of the weigh-station. The sound came through the ceiling beams and packed earth as a low, continuous tapping, like fingers spread across the entire building.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then a man spoke from the other side.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: You have taken the wrong tablet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The voice was old. Not weak. Worn smooth by repetition.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: The grain exemptions are two shelves to your right,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: The inheritance appeals are behind you. The tablet in the woman's hands belongs in a locked drawer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's fingers tightened around the clay.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo raised her voice just enough to carry through the door.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: I have spent thirty-one years listening to people become quiet on the other side of it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The key entered the lock again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg lowered the spear point toward the top of the steps.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lamplight spilled down the three narrow steps and spread across the archive floor in a weak amber wedge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A single man stood above them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He wore the undyed robe of a lower archive custodian. The cloth hung loosely from narrow shoulders bent forward by years spent over tables. Ink stained the first two fingers of his right hand all the way to the nails. His hair had gone almost entirely white, though his eyebrows remained dark and heavy over deep-set eyes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked first at BAH-lahg's spear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His gaze settled on the ledger tablet pressed against Ninsun's chest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: I know the space where the name used to be.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg lifted the spear point until it hovered level with the man's throat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: The true answer has been corrected six times.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun brought the tablet into the lamp's reach.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This says he kept the lower cistern stair.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The writing along the margin had softened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At first Zeek thought rain had found its way into the chamber, but the tablet was dry. The old clay had begun to darken around the smallest wedges. Their edges rounded before his eyes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She shifted the tablet toward the light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first line contracted into itself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wedges drew closed as though pressed from beneath by an invisible thumb. Clay rose into the incisions, filling them without leaving a seam.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun scraped at one sign with her nail.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg glanced from the tablet to the custodian.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The old man did not look at him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: POTTER BY TRADE. KEEPER OF THE LOWER CISTERN STAIR BY HEREDITARY OBLIGATION.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The last word collapsed first. Then the line before it. The clay smoothed itself from right to left, erasing the sentence faster than Ninsun could trace it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She pulled her copied scrap from inside her robe and unfolded it with one hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The final line on the tablet held.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: PROPERTY EXEMPT FROM LEVY WHILE SEVENTH ACCESS REMAINS SEALED.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The signs trembled in place like insects pinned to the clay.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The tablet became blank except for the ordinary tax figures on its face.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The custodian watched her copied scrap.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: That is why the drawers are locked,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His eyes moved toward the seven narrow drawers fitted into the far wall.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: To stop people from noticing that the records do not remain the same.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A heavy tread crossed the storage room above them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Someone dragged one of the broken scales aside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The old custodian did not answer.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: Two temple guards and a clerk who believes authority improves when repeated loudly.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That's not an answer I enjoy.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: It is the answer the room has.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek felt the linen around his left hand tighten as his fingers curled.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: I opened this door for him.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: Long enough ago that I still believed records were safer than people.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stepped closer to the bottom stair.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The custodian looked past him toward the locked drawers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Each drawer had a bronze faceplate darkened by age. Six bore district codes. The seventh had no writing at all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Only a shallow depression where a seal had once been hammered flat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He wasn't born when those ledgers were written.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: I told him the same thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The guard above came closer. His boots struck the floor directly over the archive door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His shadow stretched down the steps, long enough to reach the seven drawers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: After that, the archive began remembering him differently.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: It means some ledgers placed him in districts he had never visited. Some listed debts older than his grandfather. One recorded his death.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: Three years before he came here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The custodian stepped backward onto the storage-room floor and raised his voice.

lines.speaker: Archive Guard
lines.text: You've been down there too long.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: I am old. Everything takes too long.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The guard muttered something to the clerk. Their footsteps moved away, but not far.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mardu looked down at the four of them.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: You have perhaps half a minute before curiosity defeats laziness.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo slid her knife back into its sheath.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: I can prevent them from entering.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That is not the same thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mardu reached beneath his robe and removed a narrow bronze key.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was too long for the archive lock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun caught it against her chest with the blank tablet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked around the windowless chamber.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: Water dislikes bureaucracy. The builders gave it a private route.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mardu pointed toward the shelves behind en-HEH-doo.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: The one the temple admits happened.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: The ledgers tied with yellow cord.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo found the bundle and pulled.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The shelf behind it moved half a finger's width.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg crossed the chamber in two strides, set his shoulder against the wood, and shoved. The entire lower section slid inward with a grind of stone beneath timber.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Cold, wet air entered the archive.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind the shelf lay a rectangular opening barely high enough to crawl through. Black water moved along the bottom in a shallow, steady sheet.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Smells like an animal died in there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mardu looked down from the doorway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The door shifted under a hand from the other side.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He pulled the archive door shut.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wedge of lamplight narrowed over the steps.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His eyes met Zeek's for one final moment.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: Your father did not ask what was beneath the city,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Mardu
lines.text: He asked what the city was built on top of.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A fist struck the wood from above.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The custodian's voice came muffled through the door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned toward the locked drawers.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: And three men are standing above us.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We have a copy of a margin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stared at the blank-faced seventh drawer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The blow against the archive door came again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg caught Ninsun by the upper arm and steered her toward the opening.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She dropped to her knees and pushed the copied ledger scrap deep inside her robe. The blank tablet she left on the floor.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It was evidence ten breaths ago.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is not the same thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Black water closed over her hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo followed, keeping one shoulder raised to protect her satchel from the flow. BAH-lahg thrust his spear into the tunnel ahead of him and crawled after her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A crack split down from the upper hinge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The custodian said something Zeek could not hear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The guard answered with a curse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek turned toward the seventh drawer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen pulsed once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A slow pressure spread through his palm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The bronze faceplate on the drawer gave a faint click.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From inside the culvert, BAH-lahg's voice came back through the dark.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Another crack opened in the archive door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Its blank face reflected no light, yet he could see the outline of his wrapped hand in it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Five dark fingers pressed outward from the other side of the bronze.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The archive door split near the lock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek dropped to his knees and entered the culvert.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg seized his forearm and pulled him forward just as the archive door burst open behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It swung back across the opening.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A hand reached through before the shelf closed. The guard's fingers scraped against Zeek's boot.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg drove the butt of his spear backward.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For several moments, the only sounds were water, breath, and the guard screaming on the other side of the wood.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The culvert was too narrow to turn around. Zeek moved on his hands and knees, his shoulders scraping the damp brick. Water flowed toward him, carrying grit, bits of straw, and the sour smell of rotting grain. The satchel at his side dragged against the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That is exactly what I'm trying to ensure.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg muttered a curse and continued.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek braced his hands, but the current caught the lower half of his body and dragged him forward. His knees struck the lip. He slid down a steep clay chute slick with runoff.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He dropped perhaps six feet and landed in water deep enough to reach his thighs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg caught him before he fell backward.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.note: Whispered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They stood in a buried drain wide enough for two people to walk abreast. A curved brick ceiling vanished into darkness in both directions. Rainwater ran along a central channel, quick and black beneath the weak light en-HEH-doo had uncovered from her shuttered lamp.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, the chute ended in a square opening high in the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Short horizontal cuts appeared at regular intervals along the drain. Some had numbers beside them recording flood heights. Others had been crossed out. Newer marks had been cut lower than older ones even though the channel floor had not changed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg wiped water from his beard.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I was worried we might find something sensible.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This was cut twelve years before the one above it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: No. The record says the drain became deeper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The bricks ahead appeared to slope gently upward. The water ran toward them anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She lowered the lamp until the flame reflected in the current.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The water climbed the incline in a smooth black ribbon.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I would like to return to the part where guards were trying to arrest us.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A heavy impact came from the chute behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun pointed toward the rising channel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked toward the opposite direction.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It means nobody came back to measure it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek took the lamp from en-HEH-doo.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The drain narrowed after twenty paces. The curved ceiling lowered until BAH-lahg had to bow his head. Water pressed against their shins, flowing steadily in the same impossible direction.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek held the lamp close to the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A few survived only as fragments.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The name had been cut near knee height.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not in the formal hand of the ledger clerk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The signs were broad and uneven, made by someone more accustomed to clay than stone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beneath them, a smaller line remained intact.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She wiped algae away with her sleeve.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked back toward the chute.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: 'Until they used my name as the key.'

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Enough to strike their knees at once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lantern flame bent toward the dark ahead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's satchel moved against his hip.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The satchel struck his side again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, voices entered the drain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The guards had reached the chute.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A lamp appeared far back along the passage.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun examined the wall beside Ammaru's name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mortar around one brick differed from the rest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg shoved the spear into Zeek's hands and struck the brick with the heel of his palm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A rectangular section of wall gave way with a wet grinding sound. Cold evening air rushed through the opening, carrying rain, smoke, and the smell of frying onions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg widened the gap and looked through.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo climbed first. BAH-lahg made a step with his hands and lifted her through. She disappeared into the rain. Ninsun followed, protecting the copied margin beneath her robe. Zeek handed the lamp out and pushed the satchel ahead of him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal struck the leather again.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Get that thing out of the drain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He emerged behind a row of abandoned grain jars stacked against the weigh-station's rear wall. en-HEH-doo caught his arm and pulled him clear. BAH-lahg came through last, dragging the loose bricks back into place from outside as best he could.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A guard shouted within the drain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg set one shoulder against the repaired section.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rain had thinned to a greasy mist. Water ran along the gutters in narrow gray streams. Porters clustered beneath awnings near the front of the weigh-station, complaining about delayed grain tallies and failed roof tiles. No alarm had reached them yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo pulled her shawl over the lamp.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Running tells people they should care.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: A guard with a broken hand may also mention it.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Then look uninteresting until he does.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They crossed behind two wagons and joined the foot traffic heading toward the lower districts.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek kept the satchel under his cloak.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal thumped once against his ribs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They disappeared into the evening crowds.
